proposed: Loss-of-function mutation of the RB1 gene on chromosome 13q is the characteristic molecular abnormality in retinoblastoma, suggesting that loss (rather than activation) of the Rb gene leads to tumor development.
why: Dropped visible 13q14 deletions in some tumors, which the quote does not mention; kept RB1 loss of function on 13q in retinoblastoma.

proposed: In one study, aberrant promoter methylation of p16 was seen in at least one bronchial epithelial site from 44% of cases and controls.
why: Dropped methylation-sensitive PCR, small biopsies, smokers and preinvasive lesions; the quote only reports p16 promoter methylation in bronchial epithelial sites.

proposed: Beyond DNA methylation and histone modifications, the chromatin remodeler HELLS has been reported to silence multiple tumor suppressor genes in HCC by altering nucleosome occupancy at the NFR and enhancer.
why: Narrowed from chromatin remodeling complexes in general to HELLS in HCC, the only case in the quote.

proposed: The p16 gene resides on chromosome 9p (9p21.3) and is frequently mutated or deleted in a wide variety of tumors.
why: Location 9p21.3 and frequent mutation or deletion in many tumors are quoted; LOH is not mentioned, so it was dropped.

proposed: Among the earliest events in the colorectal tumor progression pathway is mutation of the APC gene, as part of early Wnt/β-catenin pathway activation reported in 90% of sporadic cases; the Vogelstein model lists APC alteration first among sequential drivers.
why: Dropped 'most common'; the 90% figure is for Wnt pathway activation including APC mutations, and APC is listed first in the Vogelstein model. No quote gives APC's own frequency.

proposed: BRCA1 contributes to homologous recombination repair (HRR), partly through the PALB2-dependent loading of the BRCA2-RAD51 repair machinery at DNA breaks.
why: Quote shows BRCA1 contributing to HRR; 'essential', BRCA2's own role and the unclear biochemical role of BRCA1 are not stated, so they were dropped.

proposed: BRCA1 contributes to homologous recombination repair through its role in the PALB2-dependent loading of the BRCA2-RAD51 repair machinery at DNA breaks, and BRCA1, BRCA2 and RAD51 are components of one complex.
why: Colocalization at damage sites and RAD51 activation are not stated; quotes give BRCA1's role in loading BRCA2-RAD51 at DNA breaks and the shared complex.

proposed: BRCA2 binds and mediates the loading of RAD51 onto single-stranded DNA, promoting the activity of RAD51, which catalyzes DNA strand exchange, and regulates RAD51 recruitment and function at sites of DNA repair.
why: Dropped nucleoprotein filament formation and invasion of a homologous duplex, which no quote states; kept loading onto ssDNA and regulation of RAD51.

proposed: In addition, Rad51 is a homologous DNA recombinase that catalyzes strand exchange, a key step in DNA repair through homologous recombination.
why: The only quote covers RAD51's recombinase role; BRCA1 complexes, the RecA homology and genome stability are unsupported and dropped.

proposed: In addition, PTEN is a phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate 3-phosphatase and antagonizes the PI3K/AKT signaling pathway.
why: Dropped 'major'; quotes name PTEN as a PIP3 3-phosphatase and as antagonizing PI3K-AKT signaling.

proposed: In the cell, p21 is involved in p53-mediated inhibition of cellular proliferation in response to DNA damage, and binding of p21 to CDK2 leads to CDK2/cyclin E inactivation at the G1-S checkpoint.
why: Dropped p53 binding DNA and stimulating p21 production, which no quote states; quotes cover p53-mediated p21 action and CDK2 binding.

proposed: APC promotes rapid degradation of β-catenin and acts as a negative regulator of Wnt signaling, so loss of APC would be expected to allow β-catenin to accumulate.
why: Quote shows APC drives β-catenin degradation; accumulation is hedged as an expectation, and TCF4 activation and uncontrolled growth are dropped.

proposed: Among TP53-mutant cancers, more than 91% show loss of the second allele, by mutation, chromosomal deletion, or copy-neutral loss of heterozygosity.
why: The quote gives the share among TP53-mutant cancers only, not among cancers in general, so 'most of the cancers' was narrowed.

proposed: PARP inhibitors have improved outcomes in patients with germline BRCA1/2-associated breast cancer; in one trial in high-risk, HER2-negative early breast cancer, adjuvant olaparib was associated with significantly longer survival free of invasive or distant disease than placebo.
why: Dropped the DNA-repair rationale, which no quote states; kept the germline BRCA1/2 breast cancer outcome benefit and the olaparib result.

proposed: PTEN isoforms antagonize the PI3K-AKT/PKB signaling pathway.
why: Dropped mTOR and decreased proliferation and survival; the quote only states antagonism of PI3K-AKT signaling.

proposed: The APC protein is 2,843 amino acids long; it promotes rapid degradation of β-catenin (CTNNB1) and participates in Wnt signaling as a negative regulator.
why: Dropped chromosome 5q21, cell adhesion and 'main function'; kept length and β-catenin degradation with Wnt negative regulation.

proposed: The BRCA1/BARD1 heterodimer mediates the formation of 'Lys-6'-linked polyubiquitin chains and coordinates cellular pathways such as DNA damage repair, with a central role in cell cycle control in response to DNA damage.
why: Dropped centrosome function and 'enhances'; kept ubiquitin chain formation linked to DNA repair and cell cycle control.

proposed: The APC protein is 2,843 amino acids long.
why: Only the protein length is quoted; the predominant transcript and expression in adult tissues are not stated.

proposed: The PTEN gene, located on chromosome 10q23, is mutated in a large number of cancers at high frequency.
why: Quotes give the 10q23.31 location and frequent mutation in many cancers; 'missing', the named cancers and Cowden disease are not stated.

proposed: Knudson's two-hit hypothesis proposed that retinoblastoma, a childhood cancer of the retina, arises from two inactivating mutations targeting both alleles of a tumor suppressor gene, and genetic mapping studies first identified the RB gene.
why: Dropped 'first tumor suppressor gene identified' and 'prototypical'; quotes link retinoblastoma to the two-hit hypothesis and say mapping first identified RB.

proposed: BRCA2 is a tumor suppressor that is involved in double-strand break repair pathways during homologous recombination.
why: The records cover BRCA2 only; BRCA1 and 'essential' are unsupported and dropped.

proposed: PARP inhibitors including talazoparib and olaparib are indicated in BRCA-mutated tumors: talazoparib for germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative breast cancer, and olaparib as maintenance treatment of BRCA-mutated advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer.
why: Narrowed from four approved drugs to the two with label quotes; rucaparib, niraparib, pancreatic cancer and HRD are not quoted.

proposed: Mutations in the tumor suppressor BRCA1 gene are responsible for approximately 40% of inherited breast cancers and more than 80% of inherited breast and ovarian cancers.
why: Quote covers BRCA1 only and gives inherited-cancer percentages; BRCA2 and 'strongly associated' are dropped.

proposed: At least one clinical trial has investigated a PARP inhibitor in combination with a PD-1 inhibitor: a phase II open-label study of niraparib alone or with the anti-PD1 inhibitor TSR-042 in recurrent endometrial cancer, listed as active, not recruiting.
why: Replaced 'several trials currently underway' with the one trial that names a PARP inhibitor plus anti-PD1, with its listed status; the cervical cancer trial does not name PD-1.

proposed: Different compounds have been identified that act as inhibitors of MDM2, either by directly binding to MDM2 or by modifying p53 with phosphorylation.
why: Quotes say different compounds inhibit MDM2 by binding it or modifying p53; they do not state that compounds were developed to target the p53-MDM2 interaction specifically.

proposed: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors selectively kill BRCA1/2-deficient cancer cells by inducing synthetic lethality, and tumors in patients with germline BRCA1 or BRCA2 mutations are sensitive to PARP inhibitors because of a specific DNA repair defect.
why: Dropped the claim that the concept led to PARP inhibitor development and the PARP1-specific mechanism; kept synthetic lethality in BRCA1/2-deficient cells and germline tumor sensitivity.

proposed: One molecule in this category is nutlin-3, an inhibitor of the interaction between MDM2 and p53.
why: Dropped 'first', the large in vitro screens and the p53-binding pocket mechanism; the quote only calls nutlin-3 an MDM2-p53 interaction inhibitor.

proposed: There are even hereditary cancers, such as Li-Fraumeni syndrome, associated with mutations in the tumor suppressor gene TP53.
why: The quote associates TP53 mutations with hereditary cancers such as Li-Fraumeni syndrome; 'germline' and 'loss of function' are not stated.

proposed: Loss of DNA mismatch repair activity causes a hypermutable instability phenotype, and in one study MCPH1 deficiency promoted genomic instability and increased cancer susceptibility.
why: Narrowed 'DNA damage repair deficiency' to the two cases quoted; oncogenic transformation is replaced by increased cancer susceptibility.

proposed: Unfortunately, patients acquire resistance to PARP inhibitors with prolonged administration, which limits long-term effectiveness.
why: Quotes cover acquired resistance to PARP inhibitors only; BRCA1/2 mutation context, general anti-cancer agents and selective pressure are not stated.

proposed: Mutations are frequently observed in cancer in genes that modify the epigenome.
why: Quote states frequent mutations in epigenome-modifying genes; it does not tie them to DNA methylation, histone modifications or chromatin organization.

proposed: Molecular modifications on DNA that regulate gene activity independently of DNA sequence are mitotically stable, and in one engineered setting induced DNA methylation was maintained through cell division and stem cell differentiation.
why: Dropped establishment in early development and histone modifications; quotes cover mitotic stability of DNA modifications and an engineered example.

proposed: In patients with glioblastoma and with gliosarcoma treated with temozolomide, a methylated MGMT promoter was associated with benefit from the drug and with longer survival.
why: Narrowed to the two tumor types quoted; the DNA-repair function of MGMT and the silencing mechanism are not stated.

proposed: Gene silencing by DNA methylation has been reported: aberrant DNA methylation was reported to inactivate genes in T-cell leukemia, and methylation of a single CpG locus in the RANKL and SFRP4 promoters was reported to silence them through MeCP2.
why: Dropped 'usually' and the general statement about tumor-associated genes; kept the two reported examples.

proposed: Genomic hypomethylation has been linked to the generation of genomic instability and tumorigenesis, and in one study DNA hypomethylation resulted in genomic instability.
why: Dropped proto-oncogene hypomethylation and stronger expression, which no quote states; kept the hypomethylation-genomic instability link.

proposed: In one study of bladder cancer (TCC), genetic aberrations of chromatin remodeling genes were found in 59% of 97 subjects, suggesting that aberration of chromatin regulation might be a hallmark of bladder cancer.
why: Dropped the comparison with other cancer types and 'emerging theme'; kept the bladder cancer finding and its hedged conclusion.

proposed: Genes encoding SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex subunits are collectively mutated in approximately 20% of human cancers, and mutations in the H3.3-ATRX-DAXX chromatin remodelling pathway were identified in 44% of tumours (21/48) in one study.
why: Narrowed from histone genes and chromatin modifiers generally to the two quoted pathways; impaired expression and genomic integrity are not stated.

proposed: S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) is a key cellular metabolite that acts as a methyl donor, and in various human cancers, such as lung adenocarcinoma, its level is prominently upregulated for RNA hypermethylation.
why: Dropped DNA and histone methyltransferase cofactor role and 'second most common cofactor after ATP'; the quote gives SAM as a methyl donor for RNA hypermethylation.

proposed: Frequent molecular dysregulations are found in chromatin regulatory genes in bladder cancer, and one of the most highly mutated genes, KDM6A, is an H3K27 demethylase.
why: Dropped 'the most common'; quotes show frequent chromatin gene dysregulation and KDM6A among the most highly mutated, not a ranking of gene classes.

proposed: In one cohort study, 37 microRNAs were differentially expressed in tumors from the test cohort, and five of them (miR-20a, miR-21, miR-106a, miR-181b and miR-203) were enriched in tumors from a validation cohort.
why: Narrowed from large cohort studies to one cohort study; separation of cancer subtypes by miRNA profile is not stated, and normal colon is not named in the quote.

proposed: The H19 gene was one of the first reported long non-coding RNAs and was first described as an oncofetal transcript.
why: The quotes do not say H19 was the first lncRNA causally linked to cancer, nor 'maternally expressed'; kept 'one of the first reported' and oncofetal description.

proposed: H3K27me3 is formed by the Polycomb group complex PRC2/EED-EZH2, which methylates Lys-27 of histone H3 and leads to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene.
why: Dropped 'major hallmark' and the distribution at repressive elements and gene bodies, which no quote states.

proposed: The human gene Mixed Lineage Leukemia (MLL1) is involved in multiple chromosomal translocations that are the cause of certain acute lymphoid and acute myeloid leukemias.
why: Dropped 'TrxG', 'initially identified' and 'in blood cells'; the quote only says translocations of this gene cause certain acute leukemias.

proposed: During development, mammalian cells display bivalent chromatin, with the activation-associated H3K4me3 and repression-associated H3K27me3 co-occurring at promoters of developmental genes, and in ES cells this bivalency was resolved upon differentiation.
why: Replaced fully resolved patterns, DNA methylation and acetylation with what is quoted: bivalency and its resolution on ES cell differentiation.

proposed: Mutations are frequently observed in genes that modify the epigenome in cancer, and chromatin remodelling genes were commonly mutated in one study of pancreatic neuroendocrine tumours.
why: Dropped transcriptional mis-regulation and 'not surprising'; quotes give frequent epigenome-gene mutations and one commonly mutated tumor type.

proposed: Histone deacetylase inhibitors are emerging as promising treatments for hematological malignancies, with potential applications extending to solid tumors in the future.
why: Narrowed from epi-drugs to HDAC inhibitors; the quote does not compare results or call solid tumor results a drawback.

proposed: In one study, in vitro synergism between histone deacetylase inhibitors and DNA methyltransferase inhibitors was demonstrated in preclinical models of T-cell lymphoma, and among 25 enrolled patients the overall response rate was 61% and the complete response rate 48%.
why: Dropped gene reactivation and tumor burden reduction, which no quote states; kept the T-cell lymphoma synergism and the response rates.

proposed: DNA hypomethylating agents are FDA approved for hematologic malignancies, and among the more than twenty HDAC inhibitors investigated in clinical trials, five approvals have been achieved.
why: Dropped the total of seven agents, EZH2 inhibitors and FDA-specific HDAC approvals, which no quote supports.

proposed: Azacitidine and decitabine are indicated in adults for the treatment of myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS).
why: Quoted labels list MDS only; acute myeloid leukemia and the cytosine analogue description are not in the quotes.

proposed: Azacitidine is a pyrimidine nucleoside analog of cytidine; azacitidine and decitabine are believed to exert their effects by causing DNA hypomethylation, and decitabine is believed to do so after incorporation into DNA and inhibition of DNA methyltransferase.
why: Calls them nucleoside analogs (azacitidine quoted); DNA methyltransferase inhibition is quoted for decitabine only, so azacitidine is described by hypomethylation.

proposed: By targeting DNA repair proteins on which repair-impaired cancers depend, cancer cell killing can be achieved through synthetic lethality, as when BRCA1/2-deficient tumor cells are more sensitive to PARP inhibitors.
why: The 'salvage DDR pathway' is not named in the quotes; reworded to targeting remaining repair proteins in repair-defective cancers.

proposed: Cancers frequently carry de-stabilizing mutations, and in myeloproliferative neoplasms mutations in genes involved in epigenetic regulation, splicing and signaling cooperate with the three MPN drivers.
why: Dropped 'complex disease', 'typically' and 'multiple'; quotes give frequent destabilizing mutations and one example of epigenetic-regulator mutations.

proposed: Azacitidine and decitabine are now indicated in their FDA drug labels for the treatment of adult patients with myelodysplastic syndromes (MDS).
why: Dropped the demethylating agents class statement and solid tumor efficacy signals; the quotes give only the two MDS indications.

proposed: EPZ-6438 (EPZ6438) inhibits EZH2 specifically by competitive binding at the S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) binding site.
why: The quote gives competitive SAM-site binding; oral bioavailability is quoted only for tazemetostat, so it was dropped.

proposed: Guadecitabine (SGI-110) is a next-generation hypomethylating dinucleotide of decitabine and deoxyguanosine, resistant to degradation by cytidine deaminase, with a longer half-life and exposure than its active metabolite decitabine.
why: Dropped activity in AML and high-risk AML, which no quote states; kept composition, half-life and exposure.

proposed: An FDA record for TAZVERIK (NDA213400) lists an original approval dated June 18, 2020, while a separate TAZVERIK application (NDA211723) lists an original approval dated January 23, 2020.
why: The quotes are bare approval codes; the June 18, 2020 date is supported but a second TAZVERIK record gives a different date, and epi-drug status is not stated.

proposed: Lynparza, a PARP inhibitor, is indicated for maintenance treatment of BRCA-mutated advanced epithelial ovarian, fallopian tube or primary peritoneal cancer, and for HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer with a deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA mutation.
why: Narrowed from PARP inhibitors in general to the one labelled drug with BRCA-mutated ovarian and breast indications.

proposed: RNK05047 is now in phase I/II clinical trials, indicating that selective BRD4 protein degradation may offer a viable therapeutic strategy, particularly for cancer.
why: Dropped the developer, 'PROTAC' and BRD4 as a vital cancer-driving transcription factor; the quote states trials and selective BRD4 degradation.

proposed: Tucidinostat, a subtype-selective HDAC inhibitor that inhibits class 1 HDAC1, HDAC2, HDAC3 and class 2b HDAC10, is approved in relapsed or refractory peripheral T-cell lymphoma, advanced breast cancer and relapsed or refractory adult T-cell leukemia-lymphoma, and China and Japan have approved its use.
why: Dropped 'first selective' and the claim that all four other drugs are pan-inhibitors with toxicity; kept approved indications and selectivity.

proposed: Tazemetostat is an inhibitor of the methyltransferase EZH2 and of some EZH2 gain-of-function mutations including Y646X, A682G and A692V, and is indicated for metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma not eligible for complete resection and for relapsed or refractory EZH2-mutated follicular lymphoma.
why: Dropped 'first-in-class' and the 'writer' description, which no quote states; kept the EZH2 target and the labelled indications.
